intentionalDifferences: One native warning per concrete effective GET declaration; Swagger can report flag and options separately.
Native comparison uses unprojected source; Swagger is a saved selected-version emission. Exact selected-version states were inspected for four saved targets and19 historical locations.
Existing broader Core Legacy/raw-extension bans remain separate; all four saved targets actually waive the Legacy ban.
Legitimate polling metadata alone and nonservice helpers are not affirmative declarations. Four removed pollers are retained as source history, never subtracted from the current native counts.
paths/x-ms-paths share source semantics; all four saved violations happen to be paths true flags, so corpus data alone does not establish options/x-ms-paths completeness.
